summary: A conditional answer-bank shortcut succeeds on 127/136 square-root questions (93.4%), surviving delivery filtering. Mathematics, grading, rendering and packaging checks pass. Package files remained unchanged; nothing was published or written to the database.

source_analysis.skill: Convert a radical to a unit fraction exponent by identifying its radicand and root index.
reasoning_steps: Identify radicand x and index n, using n=2 for an unindexed square root.
Select the expression preserving the radicand as base and placing the index in the denominator.
invariants: Forward, one-step notation conversion at easy difficulty.
One radio response with five mathematical choices in the captured questions.
permitted_variations: Change the radicand and higher-root index independently.
Change which eligible base/index assignment is targeted within a fixed bank.
Reorder choices while preserving mathematical correctness.
Use positive decimal radicands when conversion requires copying rather than evaluation.

source_replay.details: All three captured question banks, containing 15 choices, replay successfully. Available solutions match after harmless formatting normalization. Missing captured fields are explicitly distinguished from inferred content.

math.details: Independent exact arithmetic verifies 351 initial records and 2,560 expanded trial records, plus source replay: distinct choices, unique correct answer, and consistent solution substitutions and conclusions.

variety.details: Capacity runs cover all 126 supported semantic targets, but ordinary sampling strongly overweights target 2 within the recognizable square-root bank containing bases 2 and 3.

scope.details: Tested variations preserve one-step forward conversion, response format and easy workload. Decimal radicands require no additional arithmetic.

grading.details: The native learner grader checked 396 responses across 188 records: 179 accepted, 217 rejected, none unresolved. Tests include every choice in controlled pairs and 136 explicit shortcut submissions.

rendering.details: All 42 actual-UI previews pass. Representative screenshots confirm readable radicals, fractional exponents, decimal bases, radio controls, worked solutions and counterfactual updates.

packaging.details: Python 3.13.5 matches the manifest exactly; no third-party runtime dependencies are required. Declared files relocate successfully. Determinism, capacity boundaries and rejection cases pass. Package hashes remain unchanged.

decision_variation.details: Choosing 2^(1/2) whenever the bank contains both 2^(1/2) and 3^(1/2), without reading the radical, succeeds 127/136 times after delivery. The comparison baseline is 50% between the two legitimate bases. Faithful easy-band selection reproduces the advantage at 299/329.

findings.description: Square-root sampling treats x=n as a separate uniformly sampled case. Since n=2, this disproportionately selects radicand 2. Within banks containing both 2^(1/2) and 3^(1/2), an answer-bank-only strategy selects 2^(1/2) correctly on 127/136 items (93.4%). All 2,560 records from 512 independent five-question batches survive captured-inventory filtering; native grading confirms 127 shortcut acceptances and nine rejections. Controlled pairs establish that both bases are valid targets under identical banks. This is a demonstrated probabilistic shortcut, not a mathematical error or perfect predictor.
